MEASURED 2026-08-26 by a CI failure, after `dec:export-once-per-pr` was read, followed, and still got wrong.

═══ THE MISREADING ═══

The rule says one commit per PR may export the design **and it must be LAST**. "Last" was read as *last among the branch's commits*. So when a follow-up fix landed after the export commit, the branch reconciled and exported a SECOND time — and that second export chained its `prev_content_hash` to the FIRST one.

CI refused it:

    FAIL LINEAGE 'docs/design/reflow2.json' does not link to the export it
    replaced: it records sha256:82e005ce... where sha256:ad8b744f... is expected.

⭐ **THE MECHANISM, WHICH IS THE PART WORTH KEEPING: CI CHECKS OUT THE PR *MERGE* COMMIT, SO `HEAD~1` IS `main` — NOT THE BRANCH'S PREVIOUS COMMIT.** The guard therefore compares the branch's final export against **main's** export. A branch may export exactly ONCE, from main's baseline, and the export's `prev_content_hash` must equal MAIN's `content_hash`.

⇒ **"Last" means last relative to MAIN, not relative to the branch.** A local `reflow2_check` passes on a two-export branch because it compares against the working tree's own history; only CI sees the merge-commit view. **The local gate and the CI gate ask different questions here, and the local one is the weaker.**

═══ THE REPAIR, AND IT IS THE DOCUMENTED ONE ═══

    git reset --soft origin/main
    git checkout origin/main -- docs/design/reflow2.json   # from ORIGIN/MAIN, never the branch
    <export once>
    <commit>

Verify before pushing by comparing directly rather than trusting the shape:

    git show origin/main:docs/design/reflow2.json | jq -r .content_hash
    jq -r .prev_content_hash docs/design/reflow2.json      # must be identical

⚠️ **AND A SECOND-ORDER TRAP THAT COST A FALSE ALARM:** `git log --name-only origin/main..HEAD | grep -c docs/design/reflow2.json` is NOT a valid count of exporting commits — `--name-only` includes commit MESSAGES, so a message that mentions the path inflates the count. Count with `git show --name-only --format="" <sha>` per commit instead.

📌 WHY IT RECURS: the release-cut procedure already carried "one commit may export and `reset --soft` is the fix when you get it wrong", learned on v0.22.0. That note describes the REPAIR and never states WHY last means last-relative-to-main. **A procedure that gives the fix without the mechanism is one somebody follows correctly and still misapplies**, which is exactly what happened here on a non-release PR the note's release framing did not obviously cover.
